sections.title: Sound of letter pi
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (pi) /pi/. Its main sound is heard in the word (pane) /ˈpa.ne/, which means bread. This letter makes two sounds in Italian speech. Both sounds are made with both lips.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Close both lips firmly to stop the air. Release the air cleanly with no voice. For the longer variant, hold your lips closed for a brief moment before releasing the air. Touch your throat with a finger and feel no shaking. Hold a finger before your lips and feel almost no puff of air.

sections.title: When to use each
paragraphs: This letter usually sounds like (aperto) /aˈpɛr.to/ in all ordinary positions. When written double between vowels, it makes a longer consonant sound, as in (cappa) /ˈkap.pa/. A double consonant is a consonant that you hold longer, or say twice. It also becomes long across words through doubling, as in (a piedi) /apˈpjɛ.di/.

sections.title: Common mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not puff out air when you say this letter. Many people say it like the p in the English word pet. That sound is aspirated, which means it is followed by a small puff of air. Keep the lips tight and let out no puff of air, exactly like the p in spot.
